properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/12/2025 to APOLLO RESOURCES LLC in Derry Township, Westmoreland county. OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/12/2025
Violation Code: OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
Violation ID: 8245157
Permit API: 129-24913
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/12/2025
Comments: On 8/12/25 at 10:34 AM, I arrived at the Kovalish 3 well to conduct a Follow Up Inspection to determine if the operator had made the corrective actions they stated they would in their NOV Response sent to the DEP on May 30, 2023. James Stiffler, Production Supervisor from Apollo Resources stated: "I was informed of this record today May 30,2023. Apollo Resources LLC was unaware that inactive status had expired on this well. This well will have to be planned to be plugged. New well head tag will be installed. MIA should have been recorded for 2022. If any questions please contact me." Well is not in, or equipped for, production. Onsite equipment consists of wellhead, pumpjack, and electric service box. All equipment is inside bushes/briars/trees to the point of being inaccessible. Review found that Annual Production Reports have been submitted, with last production shown in 2016. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 5/20/2022. Mechanical Integrity Assessment reports have been submitted for 2023 and 2024. This submittal corrects 78.103, 78.104, 78.88(A), 78.88(a), 78.88(b)1-4. The operator has not plugged the well as was stated in the Mat 30, 2023 response. Violations OGA3220(A) and 78.91(A) will be continued. The Department requests a response to this report with an anticipated timeframe for plugging.

Comments: On site for routine inspection, weather is partly cloudy and 70 degs.. There are (4) wells on the pad, the Amburke 21HC, 22HC, 2H and 5H. All (4) wells are set up for automated production. Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 9/05/2023
Comments: On Wednesday, 8/30/2023, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Mountain V Oil and Gas, Inc. P and N Coal, et al, 1 well, permit number 005-27116. The well is located in the woods off of Dam Road in Kittanning township, Armstrong county. Inspection #3580553, conducted on 7/6/2023, noted that the site access road had E and S issues that needed to be addressed. The E and S BMP's had not been maintained and surface water runoff was not being properly conveyed away from the site. This resulted in multiple areas of standing/ponded water. Inspection #3591431, conducted on 7/26/2023, noted that the operator had dug in turnouts to drain the specific areas of standing/ponded water and placed stone/gravel to stabilize these locations. These actions were minimal and areas that are not stabilized remained. The operator has placed more gravel on the access road in an attempt to stabilize, but has not re-installed the E and S BMP's along the access road and surface water runoff is still not being conveyed away from the access road. The operator's failure to re-install the E and S BMP's in order to prevent erosion and maintain stabilization on the access road has resulted in violation being cited. Violations of 25 PA Code 78.53, 25 PA Code 102.4(b)(1), 25 PA Code 102.11(a)(1), and 25 PA Code 102.22(a) are being cited for this inspection.

Comments: On 10/08/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand) Kerrick Unit OG Well Pad in Asylum Township, Bradford County. The weather was 56 degrees and partly sunny. I arrived at 1025 hours. The site appears stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There was an infiltration berm onsite. It appeared to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 190.6 us/cm- 4.15 mS/cm (photo #4 and 5). Soil was field measured for EC at ~4.00 mS/cm (photo #6). Pooled water in area of the reported release on 06/04/2025 (IR #3990710 and CTS #389602) was field measured for EC between 2.04-4.15 mS/cm. The elevated pooled water was observed behind the produced fluid tank.The DEP spoke with Expand representative Mike Deming via phone and he stated their consultants visited the site the same day and confirmed the elevated water around the produced fluid tank. The release was then reported to the DEP via the 24 hour number. Expand will begin remediation on 10/09/2025. The quantity of the release is unknown. The following reoccurring violations are cited against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)Due to the unknown quantity of the release this will be referred to Act 2 for compliance. The following violations remain open against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued.I departed at 1125 hours.

Permit API: 081-20961
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/02/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 6/1/26 a release of an unknown volume of brine-contaminated stormwater occurred outside of containment. The notification also stated that Tobias was dispatched on the morning of 6/2/26 to conduct excavation of impacted pad material. A wireline operator was working on the 5H well when I arrived on location. An aboveground storage tank (AST) is present on the pad along with a gas buster tank. Well site secondary containment consisting of a secondary containment liner, containment berms, and rig mats is present around the well heads. Fluid was present on the containment. Fluid was observed on the pad surface on the north side and on the south side of the containment. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid on the north side of the containment ranged from 1 mS/cm to 2.27 mS/cm. On the south side of the containment the soil is damp but no ponded fluid was observed. The soil EC probe gave a reading of 1.07 mS/cm where the soil was the most damp. On the containment, the EC of the fluid ranged from 700 uS/cm to 3.25 mS/cm. The rest of the well pad and surrounding area appeared very dry.During this inspection, crews were working to remove the fluid from the containment, remove rig mats from the containment, and identify holes in the containment liner. Tobias was also onsite with excavation equipment and a roll-off box. Before I left the location, Tobias began to excavate the impacted pad material and place it into the roll-off box.I met with EQT representative Zac Subra during this inspection. He said that the well site secondary containment had been installed on 5/11/26 for upcoming refrac operations on the 5H well. He also said that the AST was for freshwater to be used for hydrostatic testing of the well. He said that a workover rig has prepped the 5H well for the upcoming refrac and there had been tanks containing produced fluid on the pad at that time. He said that some volume of produced fluid must have been released to the containment. He relayed that crews had so far found 3 holes in the secondary containment liner. He said that the gas buster tank on the pad was empty.I took sample 0718-273 from the pad surface north of the well site secondary containment. I took sample 0718-274 from the fluid on the well site secondary containment.On the same day at 1203, I spoke with Rick Hall of EQT. He stated that on the morning of 6/1/26, the fluid on the pad surface was initially observed and the EC was 1 mS/cm. He said the fluid was checked again throughout the day and the EC climbed until it reached 3.2 mS/cm by the evening. He said they took a sample of the fluid at that time. He said the notification to the Department was made the following morning. I recommended to him that EQT pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown release volume and he said they would. Violations noted.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack. The well's operator information and API number are not displayed on the well or elsewhere on the well site.A tank battery located 75 feet southwest of this well consists of six steel stock tanks inside of an earthen diking. There is evidence of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the diking given staining/discoloration of the gravel and elevated specific conductance (SPC) within the stained areas. Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 965518
Permit API: 015-23540
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/17/2022
Comments: On 8/17/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection in response to a spill at the Chesapeake MTL well site. The spill Complaint ID 366296 was received by the department on 8/17/2022. It was 75 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. The spill was reported as an estimated 40 gallons of produced water released to the ground due to a dump line failure on the produced water tank. The initial impacted area was reported as 5'x5'. When I arrived on location, i viewed the area around the production tank. A flow back tank was nearby, a vacuum truck was being set up near the production tank and a man lift was next to the tank. I witnessed orange paint on the ground enclosing an estimated 6'x8' foot area on the north side of the tank with dark-stained ground and enclosing an estimated 20'x20' area on the south side of the tank with lighter stained ground.I met Chesapeake's production manager Gordon Fleming. He said that he did not know the specifics of the spill but that the four wells were shut in and a crew was on site to vacuum the liquids and solids out of the production tank. The tank was going to be moved to a temporary location so the spill area, including the area under the tank, could be excavated. Gordon said that the flowback tank was going to be used for production fluids while the equipment and area associated with the spill were excavated, cleaned, repaired, and put back into service. While the vac truck crew was setting up, I viewed the contaminated area. I field tested the soil in the area marked off on the north side of the tank for conductivity with results of 1,720 uS next to the north side of the tank, 718 uS 6 feet to the northwest and 4 uS 5 feet to the northeast. Gordon put me in contact with Chesapeake's Environmental Representative Danielle Schaad who reported the following: The spill was witnessed by the lease operator who was in the process of stimulating the wells and was unloading fluids from the wells to the production tank. The piping above the tank washed out, causing the release. After reporting the spill, Chesapeake brought a drone to location to observe the area around the production tank from the air in order to visibly determine the extent of the spill. The orange paint on the ground marked the visual extent of the contamination. After the vac crew cleans the tank, it will be moved to the side, away from the contaminated area. Creston Environmental is being mobilized to the site and expected to start testing and excavating the contaminated area on 8/18/2022 at 8:00 hrs. Danielle said that Chesapeake was holding with the 40-gallon estimation of the spill until Creston Environmental is able to determine the extent of contamination and give a better estimation. The release of production fluid to the unprotected pad surface constitutes a violation of Section 402 of the Clean Streams Law, of 78A57(a) for improper control, storage and disposal of production fluids and SWMA 301 for improper management of residual waste. The department also recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a.66 due to the extent of the contamination and the estimation being close to the 42-gallon action level.I left the site at 16:10 hrs.On 8/18/2022 at 14:30 I arrived back at location to view the progress with the excavation. During the visit, I took pictures 14-21.I met with Danielle Schaad and with Creston Environmental Andrew Steffe. The excavated area was 35'x16'x2' and field tested at 995 uS conductance or less. Samples for laboratory testing were collected. Danielle did report that Chesapeake would pursue Act 2 Remediation. I did witness the excavated material piled up on plastic secondary containment. I did request a copy of the manifest upon disposal. As I was leaving the site, the excavated area was being filled in with clean material.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2023
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 995091
Permit API: 053-29816
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack that appears to have been recently produced. A sticker is posted on the pump jack displaying the operator's information, the well's API number is written on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. An approximate 2' x 5' area of vegetation and soil are stained with a coating of crude oil on the well site from the apparent repeated venting of this well into the atmosphere. The same practice is prevalent at a majority of the well sites on the Warrant 2980 lease and will be addressed in a separate inspection report. A tank battery that is located approximately 250' southeast of well consists of four steel and six plastic storage tanks inside of an earthen diking. There are several areas of stained gravel near the tanks (and at a compressor that is also located inside of the diking) which is indicative of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the containment.The exterior (southern) wall of the diking is void of vegetation and the specific conductance (SPC) is elevated (3800 uS/cm per field meter). It appears that the production fluid that has been released into the gravel inside of the tank battery diking has migrated through the southern wall of the containment and into a roadside ditch that flows south towards a cross culvert approximately 200 feet south of the well. Stressed vegetation, elevated SPC readings and abundant deer tracks are present in the ditch between the tank battery and the cross culvert and continue in a channel down to the next lease road (near 053-29533) approximately 300 feet beyond the culvert outlet.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29907, 053-29935 and 053-29916 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. Additional E and S concerns on this lease are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29536 (Warrant 2980 #37).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8184481
Permit API: 129-28783
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 4/17/2024
Comments: This is an Admin inspection report documenting the receipt of the analytical results (attached to this report) from the aqueous samples collected during the time of IR 3742855 from the onsite unnamed stream/tributary on 4/08/2024. The final analytical sample result was received on 4/17/2024.In Sample 9560 - 367 (UV/IR) which was collected at the Potential Point of Impact in response to an observed film/sheen, the UV analysis detected a petroleum product in this sample and suggested that it was crude oil. This corroborates with the onsite unnamed stream/tributary being impacted by the spill that occurred onsite the day prior to collection of these samples, as oil was released during this spill according to the report that was submitted when it occurred.No petroleum products were detected in the aqueous samples collected upstream and downstream of this Potential Point of Impact. The remaining analytical sample results collected at the Potential Point of Impact appeared to be comparable with those collected upstream and downstream. This suggests that brine and/or other pollutants were not released into this unnamed stream/tributary, and that the oil released into this unnamed stream/tributary appeared to be contained to the Potential Point of Impact. Based upon review of these analytical sample results, additional violations are being issued as the Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted by the 4/07/2024 oil spill.
